headline: Wet, windy stretch with coastal flooding and mountain snow peaking Thursday.
summary: A busy Pacific storm track is aiming fronts at Western Washington, steered by a fast jet stream high overhead. Lows stay offshore, but each system brings rain and wind. A weak ridge of high pressure offers only brief breaks, since Washington sits too far north to benefit. Thursday looks like the peak, with a front bringing strong winds, wind advisories, and heavy rain bands. High astronomical tides, the unusually high tides from moon and sun alignments, coincide with the storms and raise flood risk along waterfronts. Heavy snow is possible in the North Cascades passes. Friday brings some easing, Saturday a brief dry break, and more systems return from Sunday. Forecasters are fairly confident about the next two days, less so about the weekend and later, when coastal flooding could return.
changes: The afternoon update shifted the peak toward Thursday and added mountain snow, with a winter storm watch for the North Cascades passes. It also warned that the wind could make holiday travel harder.
